claims.text: The as-cast (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 alloy has a coarse, inhomogeneous microstructure.
The as-cast alloy has poor load-bearing integrity and is prone to intergranular cracking.
The untreated alloy exhibits a large caloric response under applied-field and pressure-field operation.
Annealing at about 700 °C for 30 minutes followed by water quenching will promote fine, coherent grain-boundary precipitates.
The proposed treatment will refine the alloy's overall grain structure.
Thermo-mechanical processing promotes heterogeneous nucleation of nanoscale precipitates at grain boundaries.
Fine grain-boundary precipitates will deflect or blunt propagating cracks.
The proposed microstructure will inhibit crack initiation and distribute local stresses more evenly.
Grain-boundary strengthening will improve the alloy's load-bearing integrity.
The treatment will preserve the primary phase transformation responsible for the caloric response.
The treated alloy will have higher fracture toughness than the untreated alloy.
The treated alloy will exhibit less crack propagation than the untreated alloy.
The treated alloy will maintain caloric-effect magnitude and transformation temperatures within approximately ±5% of the untreated baseline.
The treatment is expected to remain effective from room temperature to moderately elevated temperatures under applied field and pressure.
Excessive annealing could cause precipitate coarsening or detrimental phase changes that alter transformation behavior.
The treated and untreated samples will be tested under identical applied-field and pressure conditions.
Failure to obtain a statistically significant fracture-toughness improvement, increased crack propagation, or a caloric-effect reduction greater than about 5% will falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The intervention is repeatedly called thermo-mechanical processing, but the specified procedure contains only annealing and quenching and identifies no mechanical deformation step.
